historical_references.reference: Kandarp is an alternate name for the Hindu god Kama, who is the god of love and desire. He is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures such as the Mahabharata and the Puranas. Kandarp is described as the son of the god of desire, Rati, and the god of love, Kamadeva. He is often depicted as a beautiful and young man with a bow and arrow, symbolizing his power to arouse desire in others.

Another reference to Kandarp can be found in the Jain texts, where he is described as a sage and a disciple of Mahavira. He is said to have renounced his divine powers and embraced Jain asceticism. Kandarp is remembered for his deep spiritual insight and his devotion to Jain teachings.
